a 0.66 fJ/cycle retentive TSCC flip-flop is presented, and the proposed flip-flop shows 5% improvement in the maximum frequency and 40% reduction in the energy/cycle compared to a conventional M–S flip-flop at 0.40 V in 28-nanometer fully depleted SOI CMOS technology.
we propose an 0.4V 0.66 fJ/Cycle Retention TSPC Flip-Flop in FDSOI technology.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, analysis, and implementation of a novel 18T retentive TSC flip-flop for ultralow voltage operation in 28nm FDSOI technology.
the design of a 0.4V, 18T TSPC FF for low-energy and ultralow-voltages.
the development of a novel retentive TSCC FF for ultralow voltage operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed FF is the most efficient FF in terms of energy/cycle and leakage power at 0.3 and 0.4V, while maintaining a high maximum clock frequency.

, for the first time, a TSPC-based FF is demonstrated to operate at 0.2 V, and that it outperforms the M–S counterpart by more than 40% in energy/cycle at 0.3 V, and by more than 30% in leakage power at 0.35 V, in a 28-nm FDSOI technology node.
the proposed TSPC FF is the most efficient design in terms of energy and area for ultralow-power operation, while the M–S FF is still the most efficient design for high-frequency operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new retentive TSC flip-flop that is based on two forward-conditioned feedback loops, which is suitable for low-voltage applications.

we have demonstrated the best performance in terms of energy/cycle and leakage power for a TSPC FF at 0.3 V, and the best performance in maximum frequency at 0.5 V, among all the FFs that we have implemented in FDSOI CMOS.

the proposed FF achieves the best performance in all the metrics considered, including maximum frequency, energy per cycle, leakage power, and power delay product, among the FFs considered in the same technology node.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed FF can achieve ultralow power operation at 0.3–0.4 V without compromising the performance of the clock divider.
a simple modification in the feedback loop of a TSPC FF enables the FF to be retentive without increasing the clock loading.
the proposed FF is the first TSPC FF to achieve ultralow leakage power at ultralow voltages.
